proved: A product-facing OpenAI stream uses the same Rust-owned native Send once disclosure, OS-vault credential boundary, fixed endpoint, timeout, and exact-call cancellation registry as the existing one-shot task.

The loopback fake provider checks bearer authentication plus stream:true and store:false, dispatches five normalized events, and produces the same bounded normalized final response and content-free authoritative run record.
Disclosure denial reads no credential, contacts no network, and dispatches no event for both one-shot and streaming execution.

The Rust accumulator bounds response text and warning counts, removes the active-call registration on terminal paths, emits camelCase event fields, and excludes prompt and credential canaries from serialized events and outcomes.
The webview receives events through one ordered per-call Tauri Channel at the sole typed invoke boundary rather than a global event bus.
The TypeScript state machine rejects missing, duplicate, out-of-order, oversized, and inconsistent events while retaining only normalized provider error codes.
The workspace renders incremental OpenAI text, usage, and warnings as an aria-live transient review and states that it is never applied to the shared draft automatically.
Anthropic, Gemini, and xAI continue through the existing bounded one-shot path instead of being mislabeled as streamed.
notProved: A live API credential, paid provider request, current provider policy behavior, output quality, latency, or cost accounting.
